decisions.reason: The source decision concerns sensor interfaces only; the independently specified LED power and data-level interface remains unchanged.
Removing sensor level-shifter footprints does not change the standalone USB regulator, source selection, or loads powered by the 3.3V rail.
The sensor logic-level decision does not change the monitored rails, monitor device, measurement position, or coverage.
The interboard connector types, pinouts, and power-distribution roles remain valid; only separate sensor level-shifter circuitry is omitted.
The source does not alter DCDC1 voltage regulation, current rating, or its role as the normal 3.3V source.
The passive buzzer interface is unrelated to the sensor level-shifter decision.
The client explicitly establishes that the 5V-powered SPS30 uses 3.3V-compatible logic and therefore requires no level shifter on its I2C interface.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The level shifter was listed as DNP (Do Not Populate) by default — just the footprint on the PCB without components soldered. The purpose was future-proofing: if someone later connects a 5V-logic sensor to the spare I2C0 or UART connectors, they could populate the BSS138s to make it work. Since all sensors in our current BOM work at 3.3V (including SPS30 and ZE08 which are 5V-powered but 3.3V logic compatible), the level shifter is not needed for any connected sensor. You can skip it entirely to save board space. If we ever need 5V-logic sensors later, we'll add a small adapter board rather than reserving permanent footprints.

decisions.reason: The source removes level-shifter circuitry but does not remove or alter any sensor, spare-port, or interboard connector in the fanout.
The BSS138 level shifter is distinct from the specified I2C pull-ups and optional series resistors, whose values and topology remain unchanged.
SPS30 and ZE08 remain 5V-powered loads; their 3.3V-compatible logic does not change the boost rail or its enable behavior.
The source addresses level shifting for connected sensors and future sensor ports, not the independently specified LED daughterboard.
The possible future adapter board is conditional and does not alter the current four-board project topology.
